neighbours.label: uniqueness / exceptionality predicates (unique, uniquely, alone, an exception, exceptional), typically negated: 'not unique to X'
fire: Rising rents in the city centre are hardly a problem unique to London these days.
Researchers stress that this behaviour is not uniquely human and appears in crows as well.
Our town is far from alone in struggling to keep its small library open.
The reviewers agreed that the failed launch was an exception rather than the rule.
Few would call the decision exceptional, yet it changed how the club recruited players.
This pattern of bleaching is not unique to the reefs off Queensland.
My neighbour insists he is not alone in hating the new parking rules.
Doctors say her quick recovery was unusual but not unique among patients her age.
quiet: Rising rents in the city centre are a familiar problem across Europe these days.
Researchers stress that this behaviour is common in humans and appears in crows as well.
Our town is one of many struggling to keep its small library open.
The reviewers agreed that the failed launch followed a long run of similar delays.
Few would call the decision surprising, yet it changed how the club recruited players.
This pattern of bleaching is widespread on the reefs off Queensland.
My neighbour insists most people hate the new parking rules too.
Doctors say her quick recovery was typical among patients her age.

notes: Top: 'not uniquely American', 'not unique to', 'Kansas is alone in', 'an exception'. - pole is the opposite side: sameness ('the same way', 'similar').
